result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial road with sidewalks directly adjacent to the travel lanes, lacking any physical buffer or pedestrian refuge. The environment is designed primarily for vehicle throughput, featuring long crossing distances and utility poles that obstruct the walking path.

hazards.name: High-speed road design
hazards.description: The wide, straight multi-lane configuration encourages high vehicle speeds immediately adjacent to the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the moving traffic.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed within the walking path, narrowing the effective width for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes to slow traffic and provide space for a median or bike lanes.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Add a planting strip with trees between the curb and the sidewalk to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

result.summary: The environment features a buffered sidewalk along a commercial frontage, but the adjacent roadway is wide with multiple lanes and no visible pedestrian crossings. The presence of a large parking lot and drive-thru access points creates potential vehicle-pedestrian conflict zones.

hazards.name: Wide multi-lane roadway
hazards.description: The road has multiple lanes which encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases crossing distance for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Driveway conflict points
hazards.description: Vehicle access points to the commercial property cross the sidewalk, creating potential conflict zones.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crossing with high-visibility markings and signage if pedestrian demand warrants it.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees in the buffer zone to provide shade, improve aesthetics, and create a psychological narrowing of the road to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to encourage slower driving speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a wide, auto-oriented arterial with four travel lanes and no marked crossings visible. While sidewalks exist on both sides, they are compromised by utility pole obstructions and frequent driveway curb cuts that prioritize commercial vehicle access over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide four-lane roadway lacks any marked crossings or refuge islands, forcing pedestrians to cross a long distance unprotected from high-speed traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly within the sidewalk path on the right side, reducing the effective width and creating obstacles for those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Frequent Vehicle Conflict Points
hazards.description: Multiple wide driveway curb cuts for commercial parking lots create frequent points of conflict where turning vehicles cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides along the sidewalk

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks and Signage
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility 'continental' striping and pedestrian warning signs to define safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Construct a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time, significantly improving safety on wide roads.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Curb Radius Reduction
interventions.description: Reduce the number and width of driveways to minimize conflict points and slow down vehicles entering or exiting commercial properties.
